text: In March 2021, the container ship $\textbf{Ever Given}$ ran aground in the $\textbf{Suez Canal}$, blocking one of the world's most vital maritime $\textbf{Trade Routes}$ for six days.
explanation: The blockage disrupted global supply chains, costing billions of dollars in delayed trade and highlighting the fragility of this chokepoint.

text: In June 2021, the $\textbf{National Geographic Society}$ officially recognized the $\textbf{Southern Ocean}$ as the world's $\textbf{Fifth Ocean}$, encircling Antarctica.
explanation: While scientists had long recognized it, this official declaration standardized maps to show the unique body of water defined by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current.

text: The $\textbf{Cumbre Vieja}$ volcano erupted in late 2021 on the island of $\textbf{La Palma}$, part of the $\textbf{Canary Islands}$ archipelago belonging to $\textbf{Spain}$.
explanation: The eruption lasted for 85 days, destroying thousands of buildings and altering the island's geography with new lava flows.

text: The $\textbf{Pacific Northwest}$ Heat Dome of 2021 caused record-breaking temperatures, contributing to a devastating wildfire that destroyed the village of $\textbf{Lytton}$ in $\textbf{British Columbia}$.
explanation: Lytton set a Canadian national heat record of 49.6°C (121.3°F) just days before the fire occurred.

text: The $\textbf{COP26}$ climate summit was held in $\textbf{Glasgow}$, the largest city in $\textbf{Scotland}$, to negotiate global efforts to limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius.
explanation: Glasgow is situated on the River Clyde and has a history as a major industrial and port city.

text: For the first time on record, in August 2021, $\textbf{Rain}$ fell at the summit of the $\textbf{Greenland Ice Sheet}$, a location that normally only experiences $\textbf{Snow}$.
explanation: This alarmed climate scientists as it indicated significant warming in the Arctic region, accelerating ice melt.

text: In 2021, the Caribbean nation of $\textbf{Barbados}$ officially became a $\textbf{Republic}$, removing Queen Elizabeth II as head of state and electing its first $\textbf{President}$.
explanation: This transition marked a significant shift in the political geography of the Caribbean Commonwealth nations.

text: Hurricane $\textbf{Ida}$ made landfall in $\textbf{Louisiana}$ as a Category 4 storm in 2021, exactly 16 years after Hurricane $\textbf{Katrina}$ devastated the same region.
explanation: Ida caused catastrophic damage to the power grid and significant flooding, later causing remnants to flood New York City.

text: The $\textbf{La Soufrière}$ volcano erupted explosively in April 2021, blanketing the Caribbean island of $\textbf{Saint Vincent}$ in heavy ash.
explanation: The eruption forced the evacuation of the northern part of the island (Saint Vincent and the Grenadines).

text: Severe winter storms in February 2021 caused a massive failure of the power grid in $\textbf{Texas}$, exposing the vulnerability of its independent $\textbf{Energy Infrastructure}$.
explanation: The 'Texas Freeze' brought record low temperatures to a region ill-equipped for such extreme cold.

text: The $\textbf{Danube River}$ flows through $\textbf{Budapest}$, the capital of $\textbf{Hungary}$, separating the historic districts of Buda and Pest.
explanation: The river is a central feature of the city's geography and history.

text: The $\textbf{Great Green Wall}$ is an African initiative intended to combat $\textbf{Desertification}$ in the $\textbf{Sahel}$ region by planting a wall of trees across the continent.
explanation: The project aims to restore degraded landscapes and prevent the southward expansion of the Sahara Desert.

text: The $\textbf{Colorado River}$ flows through the $\textbf{Grand Canyon}$ in Arizona, carving the massive geological structure over millions of years.
explanation: The river is a crucial water source for the US Southwest, though it faces severe drought challenges.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Malacca}$ connects the $\textbf{Andaman Sea}$ (Indian Ocean) to the $\textbf{South China Sea}$ (Pacific Ocean).
explanation: It is one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world.

text: The $\textbf{Nullarbor Plain}$ is a vast, arid, almost treeless area of limestone bedrock in southern $\textbf{Australia}$.
explanation: The name comes from the Latin 'nullus' (no) and 'arbor' (tree).

text: The $\textbf{Pamir Mountains}$, known as the 'Roof of the World', are located primarily in $\textbf{Tajikistan}$, at the junction of the Himalayas and other ranges.
explanation: They are among the world's highest mountains.

text: The $\textbf{Okavango Delta}$ in $\textbf{Botswana}$ is a unique inland delta where the river terminates in the $\textbf{Kalahari Desert}$ rather than flowing into the sea.
explanation: This seasonal flooding creates a lush habitat for wildlife in the middle of a desert.

text: The $\textbf{Bosphorus Strait}$ in $\textbf{Istanbul}$ connects the $\textbf{Black Sea}$ to the $\textbf{Sea of Marmara}$.
explanation: It marks part of the continental boundary between Europe and Asia.

text: The $\textbf{Patagonian Desert}$ is the largest desert in the Americas, located primarily in $\textbf{Argentina}$ and bounded by the $\textbf{Andes}$ to the west.
explanation: It is a cold desert formed by the rain shadow of the Andes Mountains.

text: The $\textbf{Sargasso Sea}$ is the only sea in the world without a $\textbf{Land Boundary}$, defined instead by $\textbf{Ocean Currents}$ in the North Atlantic.
explanation: It is bounded by four currents: the Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Current, Canary Current, and North Equatorial Current.

text: The $\textbf{Tigris River}$ flows south from the mountains of southeastern Turkey through $\textbf{Iraq}$ and empties into the $\textbf{Persian Gulf}$.
explanation: Along with the Euphrates, it defines the historical region of Mesopotamia.

text: The $\textbf{Apennine Mountains}$ form the physical backbone of peninsular $\textbf{Italy}$, running from the north to the south.
explanation: They stretch about 1,200 km along the length of the Italian peninsula.

text: The $\textbf{Lake Victoria}$ is the largest lake in $\textbf{Africa}$ by area and the second-largest freshwater lake in the world.
explanation: It is shared by three countries: Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Gibraltar}$ is the entry point to the $\textbf{Mediterranean Sea}$ from the Atlantic Ocean, bordered by $\textbf{Spain}$ and $\textbf{Morocco}$.
explanation: The Rock of Gibraltar (UK territory) overlooks this strategic strait.

text: The $\textbf{Karakoram Range}$, which spans the borders of Pakistan, India, and China, contains $\textbf{K2}$, the second-highest peak in the world.
explanation: This range is known for its high concentration of peaks over 8,000 meters.

text: The $\textbf{Arctic Circle}$ is the parallel of latitude that runs approximately 66.5° North of the $\textbf{Equator}$.
explanation: It marks the southern limit of the area where the sun does not set on the summer solstice.

text: The $\textbf{Sierra Nevada}$ is a mountain range in the Western United States, primarily located in the state of $\textbf{California}$.
explanation: It is home to Yosemite National Park and Lake Tahoe.

text: The $\textbf{Orinoco River}$ is a major river system in South America, flowing mostly through $\textbf{Venezuela}$ and part of Colombia.
explanation: It is one of the longest rivers in South America.

text: The $\textbf{Great Basin Desert}$ covers much of the state of $\textbf{Nevada}$ and is known for its cold winters and basin-and-range topography.
explanation: It is the largest desert in the United States.

text: The $\textbf{Severn River}$ is the longest river in the $\textbf{United Kingdom}$, rising in Wales and flowing into the Bristol Channel.
explanation: It is slightly longer than the River Thames.

text: The $\textbf{Isle of Man}$ is a self-governing British Crown Dependency located in the $\textbf{Irish Sea}$ between Great Britain and Ireland.
explanation: It is not part of the United Kingdom but is a possession of the Crown.

text: The $\textbf{Mekong River}$ forms a major part of the border between $\textbf{Laos}$ and $\textbf{Thailand}$ before flowing into Cambodia and Vietnam.
explanation: It is the lifeblood of Southeast Asia, supporting millions with fishing and agriculture.

text: The $\textbf{Atlas Mountains}$ stretch across northwestern Africa, extending through Morocco, $\textbf{Algeria}$, and Tunisia.
explanation: They separate the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines from the Sahara Desert.

text: The $\textbf{Bay of Bengal}$ is the largest bay in the world, located in the northeastern part of the $\textbf{Indian Ocean}$.
explanation: It is bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Sri Lanka.

text: The $\textbf{Drakensberg}$ is the highest mountain range in $\textbf{Southern Africa}$, rising to 3,482 meters in Lesotho and South Africa.
explanation: The name means 'Dragon Mountains' in Afrikaans.

text: The $\textbf{Aral Sea}$, once one of the world's largest lakes, has shrunk dramatically due to Soviet irrigation projects diverting rivers in $\textbf{Central Asia}$.
explanation: It lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan and is considered one of the worst environmental disasters.

text: The $\textbf{Tasman Island}$ is located off the southeastern coast of $\textbf{Tasmania}$, which itself is an island state of Australia.
explanation: It is known for its rugged sea cliffs.

text: The $\textbf{Rub' al Khali}$, or Empty Quarter, is the largest continuous sand desert in the world, covering much of the $\textbf{Arabian Peninsula}$.
explanation: It occupies parts of Saudi Arabia, Oman, the UAE, and Yemen.

text: The $\textbf{Mackenzie River}$ is the longest river system in $\textbf{Canada}$, flowing north into the Arctic Ocean.
explanation: It drains a vast area of the Canadian North.

text: The $\textbf{Mount Kilimanjaro}$ in $\textbf{Tanzania}$ is the highest free-standing mountain in the world and the tallest in Africa.
explanation: It is a dormant volcano with three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira.
